summary.text: Paediatric patient number 11 with American cutaneous leishmaniasis refractory to pentavalent antimonials was hospitalised at Hospital Cayetano Heredia and received daily intravenous AmB-d.

Creatinine was 0.40 mg/dL at baseline and peaked at 1.1 mg/dL on day 26 of treatment, when the cumulative AmB-d dose was 14.2 mg/kg. Serum potassium was 4.3 mEq/L at baseline and fell to a minimum of 3.2 mEq/L on day 4 of treatment, when the cumulative AmB-d dose was 2.8 mg/kg.

Grade 2 hypomagnesaemia was reported that coincided with an increase in serum creatinine and hypokalaemia. AmB-d was temporarily suspended, IV magnesium and potassium supplementation was given, and treatment was resumed after recovery without further complications.

AmB-d was temporarily suspended, IV magnesium and potassium supplementation was given, and treatment was resumed after recovery without further complications.

article_limitations: Only 13 of the 20 study patients are individually identified by number in the main text (cases 4, 5, 7, 11, 12, 15, 1, 3, 6, 16, 18, 20 and 19); the roster is therefore incomplete.

Cohort statistics, Table 1, the aggregate table rows, premedication and monitoring methods, unidentified patients with alternate-day dosing or anaemia, and discussion text are not copied to individual patients.

Table 2 and Table 3 are read as the six patients with creatinine increase and the nine patients with hypokalaemia; individual CTCAE grades are given only for case 15 (grade 4 hypokalaemia) and case 11 (grade 2 hypomagnesaemia).
Table 3 prints potassium in mEq/L while the text uses mmol/L; units are kept as printed and not converted.

Text says all patients achieved clinical cure at discharge, while one patient was transferred and excluded from efficacy and 19 of 20 completed treatment; no cure outcome is assigned to any individual.
Cumulative dose range in Table 1 (7.8 to 32.5 mg/kg) differs from the text (9.6 to 31.1 mg/kg); both are aggregate and neither is assigned to a patient.
The text states that hypomagnesaemia in case 11 coincided with creatinine increase and hypokalaemia, while the tables give different treatment days for the two peaks; no order is asserted.
The supplement lists per-patient age, sex, lesion and baseline laboratory data for all 20 patients; it is reviewed in the separate supplement review, not copied into this annotation.
Caption layer is not_inspected here; the three figures were inspected in the separate visual submission.

Supplementary 2 conflicts with Table 3 for baseline potassium: patient 1 has a dash (baseline not measured per the supplement note) versus 3.7 in Table 3 (quarantined as review-only), and patient 20 has 3.78 versus 3.7 in Table 3 (kept as printed, ambiguity recorded).
Fig. 3B scatter points sit slightly above several one-decimal Table 3 minimum potassium values; chart readings are kept in the visual submission only and table values are the annotation values.

The patient transferred during the second week is identified as patient 20 only by a supplement footnote; the main text does not name the patient, so no transfer is recorded in the main-text annotation and the all-patients cure statement is not copied to any patient.
